definition: The longest side of a right-angled triangle: the side opposite the right angle.
The angle between two given sides of a triangle, at the corner where they meet.
In any triangle $ABC$, $\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C}$, where each side is opposite the angle with the same letter.
In any triangle $ABC$, $c^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2} - 2ab\cos C$, which links all three sides and one angle.
